rules.sentence: **Focus moves in on open and back to the trigger on close.** The first control in the popover takes focus (the popup itself when it has none); Escape or the trigger returns it to the trigger, so a keyboard user never loses their place.
**Escape and a press outside close it.** Both, every time — a popover the user cannot dismiss is a Dialog wearing the wrong name.
**It is non-modal.** The page behind is neither hidden from assistive technology nor scroll locked, and focus is not trapped: Tab leaves the popover.
**It is named by its title.** `role="dialog"` with `aria-labelledby` pointing at the rendered heading.
**Never the only copy of information the page needs.** A popover is closed most of the time; an error, a status or a value the task depends on lives on the page.

**It grows from its trigger, by transform and opacity alone.** Opened with a pointer it scales from 0.96 to full size as it fades in, pivoting on Base UI's `--transform-origin` — the point on the popup nearest the trigger — so it comes out of the button whichever side it opens on.

**Closed and reopened mid-flight, it turns round.** The motion is a transition, so a press that reopens it while it is still fading out brings the same popup back from where it is, and it ends open and at rest.
**From the keyboard it does not animate.** Enter or Space on the trigger opens it, and Escape closes it, at once.
**Under reduced motion it is at its end state.** Open is full size and opaque; closed is gone.
